{"thinking":"Draft has steep branches: the shell leaves the body going back up-left (way over 40 degrees) and the stalks go nearly vertical, one leaning backward. I'll give my review with concrete fixes.","review":"Body along the bottom from the tail is good, and one long spiral is the right call. Three things to change. First, the shell comes off the body heading up and back to the left, which is far too steep, so it would never fall. Have it peel off further right along the body, heading forward and up at a shallow angle, then curve up and over counterclockwise and spiral inward. Second, the stalk on the left leans backward and the other is near vertical. Let the body curve gently upward into the head, then have both stalks lean forward off it, each within about 40 degrees of the line they leave. Third, the end of the body has a kink where it bends up toward the head, so smooth that into a curve. Make the stalks a little longer too, since very short strokes break easily. Fix those and it's good to lock.","say":"Reviewed. Tom, the shell and the stalks leave the body too steeply, so they won't fall. {
  "thinking": "Reviewing Tom's draft: the foot line is good, but the spiral leaves the foot steeply (about 60 degrees, up and back to the left) and the two stalks leave at nearly 90 degrees, so none of those would fall. Give my one review with concrete fixes.",
  "review": "Snail shape reads well and the foot as one long run from the tail is good. Three things have to change or half of it won't fall. (1) The spiral peels off the foot going steeply up and back to the left. That's well past the shallow angle a branch needs. Have it leave the foot heading forward (to the right) and rising gently, then sweep up and over and round to the left, so the first bit of the shell follows the flow of the body. (2) Both eye stalks go almost straight up off the body. They need to lean forward off the head at a shallow angle, and the body should rise toward the head gradually instead of kinking. Make the stalks short, a bit longer than they are now but angled forward, and keep them clearly apart so they don't merge. (3) Keep the middle of the spiral a bit looser; the tight inner curl is fiddly and breaks easily. Otherwise a few joins, which is good. Once you redraw I'll do a dry run.",
  "say": "Tom, I've left my review. Mainly the shell and the stalks leave the body too steeply, so they won't fall. Redraw those at a shallow angle and I'll dry-run it.",

  "notes": "Reviewed draft 1 (spiral branch ~60deg off foot, stalks ~80deg, tight inner curl). Next: after Tom redraws, dry_run, then trace strokes. Start is at the tail left; stroke 1 along foot."
}
